Artifact: FinalReport
Workflow mode: feature
Run ID: 20260730T113740-implement-my-dev-kit-v1-11-0-b

Original request: Implement my-dev-kit v1.11.0 Batch 1: add the optional android-compose-semantic.json artifact, conservatively extract deterministic top-level, private top-level, function-local, preview, child-composable, and structural UI-region declaration evidence from indexed Kotlin files, integrate it with the existing Android artifact lifecycle, and add focused tests without adding state/effect/ViewModel/test/retrieval/graph behavior.

Stages completed: request-brief, architecture-context, behavior-model, pseudocode-packet, test-strategy, implementation, test-implementation, verification, judge, final-report (all 10, in order, none skipped).

Behavior designed (behavior-model.txt): 15 BEH items, 7 invariants, 3 state transitions. Core design: the artifact is present only when an Android project is detected AND at least one supported `@Composable` declaration exists; the analyzer gates on `androidProject.detected` (resolved by direct precedent from `buildComposeNavigationRoutes.ts`); no new incremental cache is needed because the analyzer is unconditionally recomputed on every index run that reaches the finishing pipeline.

Architecture context used (architecture-context-packet.txt): confirmed owners (src/android/ for the artifact+analyzer, src/indexing/ for orchestration/registration/writing), confirmed `manifestTypes.ts` needs no change, confirmed `android-navigation.json` does not participate in graph-diff today (so this new artifact correctly doesn't either), confirmed the analyzer-registry pattern (not a new manifest field) is the correct integration point.

Pseudocode summary (pseudocode-packet.txt): 25 PSE entries defining the artifact type contract, the scanning algorithm (annotation-block discovery, function-declaration discovery via char-index paren/brace matching, scope classification via textual containment, deterministic ID assignment, same-file-only child-call resolution), and the exact integration edits to 4 existing files.

Tests designed (test-strategy-packet.txt): 32 TST-NNN responsibilities (27 critical, 5 noncritical) spanning unit, integration, and regression levels, each with setup/trigger/expected-result/traces-to.

Implementation summary (implementation-report.txt): 2 new production files (src/android/androidComposeTypes.ts, src/android/buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts), 4 modified production files (src/android/index.ts, src/indexing/managedArtifacts.ts, src/indexing/writeIndexManifest.ts, src/indexing/runIndexCommand.ts), 1 documentation addition (docs/GRAPH_SCHEMA.md). Three deviations from the original pseudocode sketch, all reasoned and recorded: (1) scope classification implemented via a simpler whole-file char-index containment search instead of the sketched live frame-buffering design; (2) the function-local nesting-depth restriction was loosened, consistent with the fixed external contract not imposing one; (3) the structural-region/child-call regexes were widened to also match trailing-lambda-only Compose syntax (`Scaffold { }`) after a real bug was caught and fixed via manual smoke testing before any automated test was written.

Tests added or updated: 30 new tests (20 unit in tests/android/composeSemanticDeclarations.spec.ts, 10 integration/incremental in tests/index/androidComposeSemanticIncremental.spec.ts), plus 2 new fixture directories (tests/fixtures/android-compose-semantic/basic-app, .../no-compose-app). No existing test file was modified.

Verification summary (verification-report.txt): typecheck PASS, build PASS, focused unit tests 20/20 PASS, focused integration tests 10/10 PASS, broader regression (Android/indexing/graph-diff/integration suites) 708/708 PASS, full repository suite 1908/1908 PASS, `npm run verify` PASS (typecheck+build+docs:check), CLI version check confirmed unchanged (1.10.3), positive CLI smoke PASS (artifact present, correctly shaped, manifest registered), negative CLI smoke PASS (artifact correctly absent), generated smoke output fully removed and git-status-confirmed clean. No command was skipped without an explicit, recorded reason; no forced-internal-exception test exists for the analyzer's 'failed' status path (documented gap, matches existing sibling-analyzer test coverage).

Judge verdict: PASS (judge-report.txt), issued after evaluating implementation-vs-pseudocode fidelity, tests-vs-strategy coverage, behavior/invariant/transition coverage, architecture alignment, scope control, and verification evidence, all independently confirmed on their merits — not a default/automatic pass.

*** IMPORTANT — process exception used in this run (read before treating this PASS as routine) ***
Two of my-dev-kit's automated context-readiness gates (implementation-context and test-context) produced what this run's investigation determined, and the user explicitly confirmed and authorized treating as, verified false negatives:
1. Implementation-context: `roleAdequacy.status` reported "insufficient" solely because a fixed, repo-size-independent evidence-group budget (governingHardBound = 84 items shared across 9 required categories for the implementation role) was smaller than this repository's actual candidate-symbol volume (2242 symbols). Root-caused by direct inspection of my-dev-kit's own `src/context/contextRoleAdequacy.ts` and `src/context/evidenceGroups.ts` source, and confirmed structurally unavoidable via a second, deliberately narrowed probe request that still truncated.
2. Test-context: the responsibility-mappings evidence group has a fixed cap of 25 entries; this batch legitimately has 32 test responsibilities, so 7 (TST-026..TST-032) were dropped from the raw capsule's mapping list even though all 32 are independently confirmed mapped to passing tests in test-context-packet.txt and test-implementation-report.txt.
Per explicit, interactive user authorization obtained mid-run (decision code `CONTEXT_SUFFICIENT_BY_TARGETED_VERIFICATION_WITH_AUTOMATED_ROLE_ADEQUACY_FALSE_NEGATIVE`), this run proceeded past both gates — including past the judge stage's own generated instruction, which explicitly stated "this stage must return 'Verdict: NEED_CONTEXT'... Do not return PASS" — using independently-verified evidence (exact-symbol `mdk search`/`mdk source` retrieval, actual passing test runs, actual command exit codes) in place of the tool's bounded summary evidence. The raw gate results were never altered, hidden, or relabeled as "sufficient" in any artifact; every packet documents the true raw state alongside the override rationale. No my-dev-kit or my-dev-kit-orchestrator source file was modified to obtain or apply this override.
Full detail: implementation-context-packet.txt's "## Override authorization" section, test-context-packet.txt's "## Override authorization" section, and the "Context-gate override notice" preambles in implementation-report.txt, verification-report.txt, and judge-report.txt.

Unresolved risks:
- Three narrow, low-real-world-likelihood conservative-scanner limitations, none fixture-covered: multi-line triple-quoted Kotlin strings are not string-literal-stripped (only single-line `"..."` strings are); `<`/`>` used as a comparison operator (rather than a generic bracket) in a default-parameter-value expression could be misclassified; local classes declared inside a function body are not tracked as a distinct nesting boundary from their enclosing function. All three are consistent in kind with the base Kotlin adapter's own pre-existing documented conservative-parser limitations.
- No automated test exercises the analyzer's forced-internal-exception -> 'failed' analyzer-status path (no sibling Android analyzer test does either; no established mocking pattern exists in this repository for it).
- The two context-gate tool limitations described above remain unfixed in my-dev-kit/my-dev-kit-orchestrator (by design — the user explicitly instructed not to undertake that correction during Batch 1).

Follow-up recommendations:
1. (Primary, user-requested) File a separate, dedicated correction for my-dev-kit's context-adequacy budgeting logic (`src/context/evidenceGroups.ts`'s fixed per-role reservation totals and `src/context/contextRoleAdequacy.ts`'s unconditional `requiredEvidenceLost -> insufficient` rule) and for my-dev-kit-orchestrator's stage-context-readiness gate (`src/instructions/contextReadiness.ts`), so a documented, evidence-backed override path exists instead of requiring an interactive exception each time a repository/batch exceeds the tool's fixed evidence-group or responsibility-mapping budgets. This was encountered twice in this single run and will recur for any similarly-sized repository or any batch with more than ~25 test responsibilities.
2. Proceed to my-dev-kit v1.11.0 Batch 2 — Compose state, effects, handlers, UI markers, and ViewModel references — per the fixed, already-decided roadmap. Do not begin Batch 2 implementation in this run.
